# Shapes and colours

This page exists so the image questions have something to lose to.

Issue #122 was not "CLIP ranked the picture low". It was that a *source file*
about circles outranked an actual red circle for the query "a red circle", and
no figure the repository published would have moved if it had stayed that way.
A corpus of pictures on their own cannot show that: with nothing to compete,
the only image in the store wins by default and the measurement proves nothing.

So this corpus holds prose and code that use the same words the questions do.

A circle is the set of points at a fixed distance from a centre. A red circle
is one filled with red. A blue square has four equal sides and four right
angles. A green triangle has three. A checkerboard alternates black and white
across a grid. Horizontal stripes are bands that run left to right; yellow ones
are bright. A diagonal line runs corner to corner, and purple is what you get
between red and blue. A ring is a circle with its middle taken out, which is
also called a donut or an annulus, and orange sits between red and yellow. A
gradient fades from one value to another — grey fading from dark to light is
the plainest one there is.

None of the above is a picture. Every sentence in it is a plausible answer to a
query about one, which is exactly why it is here.
